selection_rule: Three source ACSL tutorial contracts selected using path/metadata and source-only contents before reading paired Rust target bodies.

cases.contract: Separate live integer pointers; a becomes 0 iff b is nonzero, otherwise a unchanged; b unchanged.
Separate arrays; each a[i] becomes its old value plus b[i]; all b elements unchanged.
Replace every equal-to-old element with new; all other elements unchanged.

comparison.source: Pinned original C and ACSL contracts, compiled unmodified with an external test wrapper
comparison.target: Pinned unchanged generated Rust, compiled unmodified with an external test wrapper; no semantic target edits allowed
comparison.reference: Independently coded conventional source-aware exhaustive value and frame-condition checker, given the identical input population
comparison.novelty_gate: Only measured decision-relevant distinctions unavailable to a fully informed conventional comparator count toward distinctive advantage.
comparison.stop_rule: Missing original source, hash mismatch, target build/binding failure or unsupported type adaptation yields UNKNOWN, never an inferred implementation defect.

negative_controls: Wrong result in the reset-true branch
Mutate vector input b despite correct vector output
limitations: The three source contracts were seen before preregistration; Rust target bodies were not.
The finite value populations are exhaustive only within the declared grids.
An observation primitive or test grammar furnished by the protocol is not autonomous new-sensor invention.
No release permission, human-intent certification, universal refinement theorem or human-review superiority follows from this experiment.
